features.description: Add `Rest bool` to core.RecordPattern (core.go), propagate p.Rest in elaborate/patterns.go:207-219, and honor it in checkPattern (typechecker_patterns.go:394-416): when Rest==true always build an OPEN constraint {matched fields | freshRow} even when scrutinee already resolves to a *TRecord; keep today's closed behavior when Rest==false. This is the confirmed structural root cause (H1) — the open/closed intent was erased at the AST->Core boundary. Instrument to confirm the IIFE param resolves to an open TRecord.

features.notes: DONE (commit 71ecde047). Root cause was DEEPER than the plan's H1/H2/H3. Three coordinated fixes: (1) core.RecordPattern.Rest bool + elaborator propagation (H1, confirmed). (2) checkPattern honors Rest ONLY for an UNRESOLVED scrutinee (lambda param): open=>{fields|freshRow}, closed=>Row:nil. A RESOLVED record scrutinee reads fields verbatim (subset match) regardless of Rest — my first attempt gated on recTy.Row==nil which broke closed arm `{name,age}` against a wider literal `{name,age,active}`; corrected. (3) THE primary site, NOT in the design doc: unifyRecord's TRecord~TRecord path rejected any field-count difference BEFORE consulting row vars, so open {name|r} vs {name,id} failed a length check and never reached row unification. Added unifyOpenRecords + recordRowIsOpen/recordExtensionRow helpers (TRecord.Row is overloaded: closed literals carry *Row{Tail:nil}, so Row!=nil does NOT mean open). Verified matrix cache-busted: all 7 shapes correct, strictness NOT reversed. gob-safe (new bool zero-values); all struct literals use keyed fields; internal/smt (RecordPattern consumer) green.

features.notes: NO CODE CHANGE NEEDED — proved unnecessary via instrumentation (as the plan anticipated). CheckCoreExpr.SolveConstraints() runs BEFORE generalizeWithConstraints, so the let-bound param's record structure ({name: t | r} or closed {name: t}) is already resolved and preserved through the scheme's Type field. Confirmed: let-bound open+extra PASSES, let-bound closed+extra FAILS, let-bound missing-field FAILS. The RowVars:[]string{} hardcode is a real latent gap but does NOT affect this bug because the row var is embedded in the record type, not a top-level quantified row. Covered by the M4 let-bound tests (ExtraField_Pass, ClosedRecord_ExtraField_Fail, MissingField_Fail).
